items.q: What two RSI papers did Code Report recap?
items.a: *The Last AI Built by Humans* (ByteDance / Tsinghua et al.) maps five stages ending at the AI rewriting its own improver. *Dream-RSI* (Google / DeepMind / Maryland) claims better discoveries **without touching the model** by dreaming new search policies over old logs.

items.q: What is an exploration policy in the AlphaEvolve loop?
items.a: At each propose / score / retry step: keep going on a slightly better attempt, restart, or treat a crash as idea-fail vs implementation-fail. Until this paper that knob was **hardcoded**.

items.q: How does Dream-RSI test a new policy for free?
items.a: Cache every attempt (code, score, crash). Replay the disk log as a simulator. Score thousands of policies. Keep the one that would have hit the best result in the fewest tries. Deploy it on the next live run.

items.q: Why is this not recursive self-improvement?
items.a: The model writing each new policy is still the **same Gemini**. It finds things it could already write, just faster. Weights move only when a **human** trains the next model on the swarm's finds.
